title: observability: add token/KV metrics, dashboard, and alert tuning for token-level cost/latency
author: Emily Chen
description:
Motivation: Improve token-level observability for KV-backed models to make cost and latency regressions easier to detect and triage. This PR introduces new metrics (token_count_by_route, kv_cache_hit_ratio_by_model, per_token_latency_p95/p99), a Grafana dashboard JSON, tuned alert thresholds, and documentation.

What changed: - New metrics exported by the serving runtime and metrics-agent: token_count_by_route, kv_cache_hit_ratio_by_model, token_cost_estimate_per_request, per_token_latency_{p50,p95,p99}. - Dashboard: dashboards/token_kv_token_level.json with panels for cost/latency breakdown by route/model, KV cache hit trends, distribution and spike detection. - Alerts: alerts/token_kv_alerts.yaml with tuned thresholds to reduce noisy paging while preserving SLO coverage. - Docs: docs/observability/token-kv-metrics.md with query examples and recommended runbooks. - Tests: unit tests for metrics aggregation and integration test that verifies metric labels emitted for simulated requests.

Checklist: - [x] Metrics instrumentation in runtime and metrics-agent. - [x] Dashboard created and validated in staging grafana. - [x] Alerts tuned with historical backtesting. - [x] Docs and runbook added. - [x] Integration tests pass.

Backfill/Compat Notes: New metrics are additive; existing dashboards unchanged. Backfill historical dashboards using the exported sample queries in docs if needed.

Rollback plan: Revert feature/observability/token-kv-dashboard-enhancements branch if alerts generate unacceptable noise; metric exports are guarded by feature flag metrics.token_kv_v2 (off by default in dedicated/private).

Related: Linear ENG-8421 (token-level cost visibility) and ENG-8502 (kv cache observability). Support ticket SUP-4312 reported noisy alerts that motivated threshold re-evaluation.
